slides.title: Preparing for infusion
text: Y set blood tubing w/ filter
With another nurse (RN), verify blood product & client ID
Blood bank # on ID matches transfusion record
Blood type & Rh matches  transfusion record & blood bag
Check expiration date on bag, observe for bubbles, cloudiness, sediment, clots

slides.title: Transfusion
text: Baseline VS prior to admission of transfusion
Wash hands put on unsterile gloves
Remain w/ client during first 15 min of infusion, check VS
How long can the blood hang for safely?
What medication is given prior to administration?

slides.title: Transfusion Reaction
text: Replace blood tubing with primed NS set
Send blood & tubing to blood bank

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client receiving packed red blood cells(PRBCs). Which of the following manifestations should alert the nurse to a hemolytic transfusion reaction? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is caring for a client receiving packed red blood cells(PRBCs). Which of the following manifestations should alert the nurse to a hemolytic transfusion reaction? Select all that apply.

slides.title: Headache. Yes.
text: Hypertension. No, the client would have hypotension.
Distended neck veins. No, this is circulatory overload reaction.

slides.title: Transfusion Reaction Symptoms
text: Hemolytic transfusion reaction: burning in the veins, facial flushing, fever, chills, HA, C/P, low back pain
Allergic reaction: hives, pruritus, facial or glottal edema, pulmonary edema, anaphylaxis
Febrile reaction: chills and fever, HA
Bacterial reaction: shaking fever, hypotension, dry flushed skin, abdominal pain, V/D
Circulatory overload: tightness in chest, labored breathing, edema, crackles
Air embolism: Cyanosis, dyspnea, shock, & cardiac arrest
Do we always stop the infusion with any of these reactions?

slides.title: Central Venous Access
text: May be inserted at bedside, OR, or PACU
Pre-flush before blood draw to prevent air
Before using, CXR to verify placement
CDC  recommends use of ultrasound guidance
- Subclavian; in Trendelenburg w/vertical towel roll b/t scapula
- Jugular; in Trendelenburg w/ head turned in opposite direction

slides.title: Central Venous Access
text: Clamp for cap changes & when not in use
10 ml syringe recommended, IVs via pump
Never force a push; draw back for blood return
Do not take blood pressure in the involved arm

slides.title: Central Venous Access Device- Dressing Change
text: Central Venous Access Device- Dressing Change
Dressing change 24 hours after insertion then every 3-7 days after (per policy)
Client in supine position w/ face away from site
Use clean gloves to remove old dressing
Apply mask(s), sterile gloves – sterile procedure!
Apply transparent drsg/occlusive gauze drsg over site

slides.title: Parenteral Nutrition
text: Cannot meet nutritional needs by oral or enteral routes
Trace elements – zinc, copper, chromium, manganese
May also contain – Insulin, Pepcid, Heparin

slides.title: Use one line/port exclusively for TPN
text: Use one line/port exclusively for TPN
Don't change infusion rate without an order…EVER
Warm to room temp 1 hour prior to admin.
Use infusion pump; monitor q 30 – 60 min
Dextrose > 10%  must be given via Central Venous Catheter
may be given peripherally( PPN) if < 10%

slides.title: TPN Guidelines
text: Monitor labs: electrolytes, LFTs, BUN/creat, Hct, glucose

slides.title: Parenteral Lipids
text: Derived from soybean or safflower oil
Follow protocols for concurrent administration w/ TPN

slides.title: Wasting Narcotics
text: DO NOT FLUSH unused medications in general.
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has determined that narcotics, methadone, Fentanyl, diazepam should be flushed due to their abuse potential.
When tossing unused medications, protect children and pets from the potentially negative effects
Crush solid medications or dissolve them in water and mix with kitty litter or sawdust , then place in a sealed plastic bag BEFORE tossing in the trash
Remove and destroy ALL identifying personal information (prescription label) from the medication container
Talk to the pharmacist if unsure

slides.title: Medication Administration
text: Subcutaneous -  drug injected into subcutaneous tissue

slides.title: Medication AdministrationIntramuscularly- drug injected into muscle
text: Medication AdministrationIntramuscularly- drug injected into muscle
No more than 3ml of solution; 1ml in deltoid
Spread skin taut with non dominant hand
Insert needle in a dart like motion in a 90-degree angle
What size needle should we use?

slides.title: Medication AdministrationIntramuscularly-Z Track
text: A technique used to administer medications that are highly irritating to the tissue
Use the air lock technique (add 0.2ml air to syringe) after medication is drawn up in syringe
Change needle to a clean dry needle if possible
The skin is pulled to the side about 1 – 1 ½  inches laterally away from site and held in this position.( with the left hand for a right-handed person)
The needle is inserted at a 90-degree angle and aspirated for blood

slides.title: The solution is injected slowly keeping skin taut for 10 seconds after giving the medication
text: The solution is injected slowly keeping skin taut for 10 seconds after giving the medication
Withdraw needle and release retracted skin
Used with Vistaril and Iron Dextran (Imferon) and Iron Sorbitex (Jectofer )

slides.title: Medication Administration Intradermal-drug injected under epidermis
text: Medication Administration Intradermal-drug injected under epidermis
Placed just below epidermis, 1/8”below skin surface
Use TB Syringe with 0.5 ml or less
Note site on skin with skin pencil – not ink or permanent marker

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed a blood transfusion. The client asks if any disease can be transmitted from the donor. Which of the following diseases can be transmitted from a donor? Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed a blood transfusion. The client asks if any disease can be transmitted from the donor. Which of the following diseases can be transmitted from a donor? Select all that apply.

slides.title: Epstein-Barr. Yes, transmitted by blood route.
text: Epstein-Barr. Yes, transmitted by blood route.
HIV. Yes, transmitted by blood route.
CMV. Yes, transmitted by blood route.
Hepatitis A. No, transmitted by oral-fecal route.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed 2 units of packed red blood cells. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement when caring for the client. Select all that apply.
text: The nurse is caring for a client prescribed 2 units of packed red blood cells. Which of the following actions should the nurse implement when caring for the client. Select all that apply.
Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same.
Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours.
Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open.
Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing.
Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots.
Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion.

slides.title: Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same. No, you need to verify units with the client's identifier information not the bags.
text: Verify that the ABO and Rh of the 2 units are the same. No, you need to verify units with the client's identifier information not the bags.
Infuse a unit of PRBCs in less than 4 hours. Yes, a unit should infuse in 4 hours or less.
Stop the transfusion if a reaction occurs but keep the line open. Yes, if a reaction occurs you should stop the infusion and KVO.

Take the vital signs every 15 minutes while the unit is transfusing. No, vitals should be taken prior to administration, every 15 minutes for the first hour, then every hour until complete. Not every 15 minutes for the entire transfusion.
Inspect the blood bag for leaks, abnormal color, and clots. Yes, blood should be inspected for these prior to administration.
Use a 22-gauge catheter for optimal flow of a blood transfusion. No, a 19 gauge or larger catheter should be used so RBCs are not destroyed by the lumen.

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Question
text: 0900: The nurse on the medical surgical unit is caring for a 32-year-old client with pneumonia. Client is afebrile, chest is clear per auscultation. Ambulated to the bathroom and voided 250 mL of clear yellow urine. The client is sitting up in bed, watching television, and sipping on juice. Reports prescribed codeine has “helped me bring up secretions from cough.” The client’s spouse is planning to drive the client home in 2 hours. The nurse is preparing discharge instructions.
Complete the following sentence by choosing from the list of options below.
The nurse should include _____ in the client’s discharge instructions.
Reminding that codeine onset is 90 minutes.
